question.text: 'Sahyadri Angels Fund' is a SEBI-registered Angel Fund (sub-category of Cat I AIF) raising capital from Accredited Investors and KMPs of the fund/manager. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations and the revised 2025 framework, which of the following is TRUE about Angel Funds?

answer.text: Maximum 1,000 angel investors per scheme, same as other Cat I AIFs
Minimum investment from an angel investor is INR 1 crore, same as regular AIFs

Angel Funds raise funds only from Accredited Investors (and KMPs of the fund/manager); no minimum value of investment by an angel investor; investment by an Angel Fund in an investee company must be between INR 10 lakh and INR 25 crore; lock-in of 1 year (6 months if sold to a third party)
Angel Funds can list units on a recognised stock exchange for liquidity

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the revised Angel Fund framework, Angel Funds raise funds only from Accredited Investors, with a carve-out for KMPs of the fund or its manager. There is no minimum investment value applicable to an angel investor. Each investment by the Angel Fund in an investee company must be between INR 10 lakh and INR 25 crore, and units of the fund are subject to a lock-in of 1 year, reduced to 6 months where the units are sold to a third party. The Trap: Option A states an investor cap that does not match the Angel Fund framework. Option B applies the regular AIF minimum investment of INR 1 crore, which is not the rule for Angel Funds. Option D is wrong because Angel Fund units cannot be listed on a recognised stock exchange. Note: Read the stem carefully: under the current framework, Angel Funds raise capital from Accredited Investors plus KMPs of the fund/manager, not from HNI angel investors generically; the investor-eligibility criterion is accreditation, not high-net-worth status.
